reuse.why: Adds one shared predicate skipsWeekendOccurrences used by getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and the schedule template, and the template reuses getNextDate for skipping; getUpcomingDates still filters weekends itself instead of sharing the weekday lookup.

duplication.why: Weekday skipping is written twice (getNextWeekdayOccurrence in shared/schedules and the filter/slice in getUpcomingDates), and the 'move only when not skipping' condition is restated in the template's getMovedDate beside getNextDate's own branch order.

placement.why: The rule and the weekday search sit in shared/schedules.ts and the frequency is carried in the parsed schedule data from rule-utils, following the existing layering (shared/schedules already imports server types).

scope.why: Focused on the daily-schedule rule; the template loop is reshaped into local closures, a reasonable but broader edit than strictly needed.

maintainability.why: Which schedules skip is defined once, but how skipping and moving interact is spread over three sites, including a double-negative noSkipWeekend argument in the template, so a future change to the weekend handling still touches several places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No shared weekend-decision function existed; all three sites now call skipsWeekendOccurrences.

disguised_duplication.where: getUpcomingDates' weekend filter repeats the idea of getNextWeekdayOccurrence in a different shape for a list, which is visible rather than disguised; the template's skipWeekend && !skipsWeekendDays repeats getNextDate's branch order openly.

one_place.where: skipsWeekendOccurrences in shared/schedules.ts decides for every path (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates in server/schedules/app.ts, createScheduleList in server/budget/schedule-template.ts) whether occurrences are skipped instead of moved, though each path applies the skip with its own code.
